skill.name: create-pr
skill.description: Guides AI agents through Sentry-style pull request creation using Git, GitHub CLI, and reviewer-focused descriptions.
skill.summary: Create draft pull requests with branch checks, concise titles, and Sentry-style review context.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced command examples, and documentation links in SKILL.md. The skill transparently instructs users to run Git and GitHub CLI commands for pull request creation; no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Repository PR templates may contain required project-specific review fields.
remediation.suggestion: Preserve required template sections unless the user explicitly chooses Sentry-only formatting.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI examples can create or modify remote pull requests.
remediation.suggestion: Remind users to confirm generated titles, bodies, branches, and PR numbers before running create or update commands.

content.value_statement: Pull request descriptions often miss context or reviewer needs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through branch checks, diff review, draft PR creation, and Sentry-style descriptions.
actual_capabilities: Checks git status and commit ranges before creating a pull request.
Finds the repository default branch with GitHub CLI.
Reviews commit history and diffs to shape the PR summary.
Creates draft PRs with structured titles and reviewer-focused bodies.
Shows how to update PR titles and descriptions through GitHub API calls.
Provides Sentry-style examples for feature, bug fix, and refactor PRs.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI and a repository with Git history.
Does not commit files; it directs users to a separate commit workflow.
Follows Sentry conventions, which may conflict with repository PR templates.
Does not validate CI results, permissions, or branch protection rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature PR
use_cases.description: Create a draft pull request after checking commits, diffs, and the default branch.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Context
use_cases.description: Give teams a consistent description structure that explains motivation, alternatives, and review context.

use_cases.title: Update Existing PR Metadata
use_cases.description: Revise a PR title or body when scope changes after review starts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Draft PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a current feature branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a draft PR for my current branch. Check the base branch, inspect the commits and diff, then write a Sentry-style title and description.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a PR Description
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the branch is ready but the description needs review context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my branch changes and write a concise PR description. Explain what changed, why it changed, and any review notes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Review-Focused PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for changes that need careful reviewer attention.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a draft PR for this branch. Highlight risky areas, relevant issue links, alternatives considered, and context reviewers cannot see from the diff.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for changing a created pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update PR NUMBER with a clearer title and body. Read the branch changes, keep required context, and confirm the exact PR before editing.

output_examples.input: Create a draft PR for a feature branch that adds Slack thread replies to alert notifications.
output_examples.output: Draft title: feat(alerts): Add Slack thread replies. The body explains grouped notifications, why threading was chosen, and the related issue reference.

output_examples.input: Prepare a bug fix PR for a null user API response.
output_examples.output: Draft title: fix(api): Handle null user responses. The body describes the crash, the new null handling, and the issue that motivated the fix.

output_examples.input: Update an existing PR after requirements changed.
output_examples.output: The updated PR title reflects the new scope. The body adds the reason for the change and preserves reviewer context.

best_practices: Confirm all intended changes are committed before starting.
Keep the PR body focused on motivation, tradeoffs, and reviewer context.
Open complex work as a draft PR for early feedback.
anti_patterns: Do not bundle unrelated fixes and features into one PR.
Do not replace repository-required sections without team approval.
Do not include secrets, tokens, or private customer data in PR text.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the agent to use GitHub CLI. Review the generated title, body, and target branch before creation.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects the gh command to be installed and authenticated.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Sentry projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but the description style follows Sentry conventions. Adjust it when your repository requires a different template.

faq.question: Will it commit my changes?
faq.answer: No. The skill expects changes to be committed before PR creation.

faq.question: Does it include a test plan section?
faq.answer: No. The skill follows Sentry guidance and focuses on motivation, context, and review notes.

faq.question: Can it update an existing PR?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for updating PR titles and bodies with the GitHub API.
